observations: Black Yamaha-branded electronic keyboard resting on an orange plastic chair, photographed from multiple angles.
YAMAHA logo visible on the keyboard body in photos 0, 1, and 2.
Small-to-standard size keys, slightly yellowed/worn, with a basic LCD display and multi-color rhythm/voice label strips typical of entry-level home keyboards (e.g., PSR-series look).
No power adapter, power cord, stand, or sustain pedal visible in any photo.
No photo shows the unit powered on; display appears dark/inactive.
Background shows an outdoor or semi-outdoor setting (cracked wall, damp-looking surface), raising environmental exposure concern.
A watermark 'LUCKY SOUNDS SERVICES LTD' appears on photos 1 and 2, suggesting a reseller/shop listing rather than an individual owner photo.

claims.evidence: Photos 0-2 show a small home-style keyboard with basic voice/rhythm label strips and a simple LCD, consistent with an entry-level model, not a professional stage keyboard or workstation.

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or may have non-functional keys/buttons
risks.proof: A video clip of the keyboard powering on, playing a few keys across the range, and demonstrating voice/rhythm buttons

risks.risk: Missing power adapter/cord, which is needed to operate the unit
risks.proof: A photo of the original or compatible AC adapter included in the sale

risks.risk: Possible water/damp exposure given the outdoor setting, which can damage internal electronics
risks.proof: Photos of the underside/battery compartment and confirmation of storage conditions

risks.risk: Exact model unknown, which affects feature set and market value tier
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the model number, usually printed near the power input or underside
risks.if_unproven: priced as base generic Yamaha home keyboard

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the model number (usually on the back or near the power jack)
Video of the keyboard powered on, demonstrating sound, keys, and buttons
Photo of the power adapter included with the sale
Photo of the underside/battery compartment to check for corrosion or damage
response.reason: Brand and general type (Yamaha home-style keyboard) are clear from the photos, but the professional-grade claim is contradicted by its basic appearance, and with no proof of power-on function or included adapter, it must be priced at worst case as an untested, accessory-incomplete entry-level unit.
